Package org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery

package org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery
A protocol-agnostic query API for filtering, sorting, and paging collections of beans (design §5).

A BeanQuery carries only raw strings: one search string of column=expression clauses in the $-language, plus raw view/sort directives, position/ limit, and an open opts bag. The clause grammar shared by search and opts is decoded by ClauseParser; the single public SearchExpressionParser then parses each clause's expression against a SearchOperatorSet, throwing BeanQuerySyntaxException on an unknown operator or a malformed expression.

A BeanQueryContext is the immutable, thread-safe half: its columns, operators and limits are fixed by a builder (create()...build(); copy() derives a variant). Per request it opens a BeanQuerySession, which may narrow the columns, override the limits and add a guard. Every query is validated into a ResolvedQuery before any engine runs it; rule violations throw BeanQuerySyntaxException (client error) and engine failures throw BeanQueryExecutionException (server error). Results come back as Pages with the counts the CountPolicy selects.

The InMemoryBeanQueryContext runs against an in-JVM collection. SQL engines live in separate modules: juneau-beanquery-sql supplies the shared JDBC context and the SqlDialect hook under org.apache.juneau.beanquery.sql. Commons carries the query API only, not the SQL dialect types.

Example:

static final InMemoryBeanQueryContext<Person> PEOPLE = InMemoryBeanQueryContext .create(Person.class) .exclude("password") .maxLimit(500) .build(); try (InMemoryBeanQuerySession<Person> session = PEOPLE.getSession(people)) { Page<Person> page = session.find(BeanQuery.create() .setSearch("age=$gt(21)") .setSort("name") .setLimit(20)); }

    The settings every engine's context builder shares.
    BeanQueryExecutionException
    A server-side failure while running a valid BeanQuery: a SQLException, a connection failure, or a column accessor that throws.
    BeanQuerySession<T>
    One unit of query work against a BeanQueryContext: the rows (or connection) to query, plus optional per-request narrowing of the context's settings.
    BeanQuerySession.Builder<T,SELF extends BeanQuerySession.Builder<T,SELF>>
    The settings every engine's session builder shares.
    BeanQuerySyntaxException
    Thrown when a $-search expression names an unknown operator or is otherwise malformed (an unclosed parenthesis, a wrong argument count, junk after the close paren, an empty expression, and so on), or when a higher-level check (column allow-list, sort keys, paging, regex policy, operator/type mismatch, an unparseable typed value) rejects a caller-supplied query.
    BeanQuerySyntaxException.Code
    Stable identity for a BeanQuerySyntaxException, independent of the (free-text) message.
    ClauseParser
    The clause grammar shared by the one search string and the one opts string (design §5.3).
    CountPolicy
    Which counts a find / findValues call computes alongside its page of rows.
    CountRequest
    What a caller asks BeanQuery.Builder.counts(CountRequest) to write onto a BeanQuery's opts (design §5).
    Counts
    The two neutral row counts a session can report: Counts.total() (the rows in scope before the query's search) and Counts.matched() (the rows that survive the search, before any page limit).
    Filter
    A resolved, engine-neutral search tree (design §7) — the ResolvedQuery.filter() replacement for the earlier flat Term/terms() list.
    Filter.And
    An AND of two or more (or, at the top level, zero) sub-filters.
    Filter.Leaf
    One resolved column=expression leaf, with the column's SearchType carried alongside for the engine.
    Filter.Not
    The negation of exactly one sub-filter.
    Filter.Or
    An OR of two or more sub-filters.

    SearchExpressionParser
